title: United Tractors shares fall 3.68% to Rp 22,925 as foreign investors net buy and broker MNC Sekuritas issues buy recommendation
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) slid 3.68% to close at Rp 22,925 on 29 May 2026, with 28.95 million shares traded (value Rp 668.35 billion) and foreign investors recording a net purchase of Rp 85.23 billion in the stock of the Astra International subsidiary. The company’s valuation improved to a price‑to‑book ratio of 0.89× and a price‑earnings multiple of 6.97× (TTM), prompting MNC Sekuritas to recommend a buy trade for UNTR with entry between Rp 22,575‑22,925 and price targets of Rp 24,225 and Rp 25,250. In its 4‑month‑2026 operational update, United Tractors reported a 25% YoY drop in Komatsu sales to 1,413 units (35% of the revised 2026 target), a 5% YoY decline in overburden volume to 321.3 million bcm (36% of target), while coal sales rose 12% to 5.5 million tons (47% of target) and nickel sales fell 1% to 697 k wmt (58% of target).

title: PT United Tractors Tbk cuts 2026 targets as capex is slashed and profit outlook weakens
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) lowered its 2026 operational guidance across most segments, cutting coal sales target to 7.5 million tonnes – about 35 % below prior expectations – and reducing capital expenditure by 27 % to US$650 million, with Pama capex slashed 50 %. The company reported Q1‑2026 net profit of Rp 1.8 trillion, down 44 % year‑on‑year, and net revenue of Rp 28.6 trillion, down 17 %, while forecasting full‑year revenue of Rp 104.52 trillion and net profit of Rp 11.57 trillion, both roughly 20 % lower than 2025. Analysts highlighted risks from delayed Martabe gold‑mine production (target 60,000 oz in 2026, 70,000 oz in 2027 versus 200,000 oz capacity) and a potential 25 % profit dip in 2027, but noted that solid global coal prices and a possible US monetary easing could support earnings. Despite the challenges, Korea Investment & Sekuritas Indonesia, JP Morgan Sekuritas Indonesia and UBS Sekuritas Indonesia each maintained buy/overweight recommendations for UNTR, with target prices of Rp 28,000, Rp 29,050 and Rp 36,500 respectively.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk faces 2026 earnings pressure after operational target cuts and 27% capex reduction
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) lowered its 2026 operational targets across most segments, cutting coal sales from Tuah Turangga Agung to 7.5 million tonnes – about 35 % below the previous goal – and reducing capital expenditure by 27 % to US$650 million, including a 50 % cut to PT Pamapersada Nusantara’s capex. In Q1‑2026 the company reported net profit (excluding non‑recurring items) of Rp 1.8 trillion, down 44 % YoY, and net revenue of Rp 28.6 trillion, down 17 % from Rp 34.3 trillion a year earlier. Analysts from Kiwoom Securities project a 15‑20 % annual revenue decline, citing the temporary shutdown of the Martabe gold mine, lower overburden‑removal targets and delayed RKAB approvals, while Korea Investment & Sekuritas Indonesia sees the current PER of about 8× and a dividend yield as attractive, recommending a buy with a target price of Rp 28,000.

title: United Tractors shares rise 2.27% to Rp 22,500 as MNC Sekuritas recommends Buy on Weakness with targets up to Rp 24,850
body: United Tractors (PT United Tractors Tbk) closed up 2.27% at Rp 22,500 on Thursday 25 June 2026, with 6.63 million shares traded (7,062 transactions) and a transaction value of Rp 148.37 billion. Foreign investors were net buyers of the stock, recording a net purchase of Rp 3.4 billion. MNC Sekuritas highlighted the stock’s attractive valuation, noting a price‑to‑book ratio of 0.87 (below 1) and a price‑earnings ratio of 32.64 annualized, and issued a “Buy on Weakness” call with a price range of Rp 21,350‑22,075, target price 1 of Rp 23,850, target price 2 of Rp 24,850, and a stop‑loss below Rp 20,875. United Tractors is described as an “anak usaha PT Astra International Tbk,” indicating it is a subsidiary of Astra International, and its shares have fallen 6.44% over the past month and 25% over the past three months.

title: United Tractors expands non‑coal mineral exposure with Nickel Industries’ HPAL smelter stakes and $70 million loan to Agincourt Resources
body: United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), an Astra Group listed company, is deepening its non‑coal mineral portfolio as its associate Nickel Industries Limited (NIC) signed agreements to acquire a 17.5% stake in PT Teluk Metal Industry for US$169 million and a 36% stake in PT Chengsheng New Energy valued at US$241.6 million, both HP‑HPAL smelters slated to reach full capacity by 2027. The transactions are funded by NIC’s internal cash and a supplemental debt option from its largest shareholder Shanghai Decent, while NIC reported 2025 nickel metal sales of 125,341 tons and an RKAB quota increase to 14.3 million wet metric tons for 2026. In parallel, United Tractors’ subsidiaries PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and PT Agincourt Resources executed a revolving loan agreement of up to US$70 million at SOFR + 1.15% per annum, maturing on 16 June 2029. Analysts note that United Tractors’ cash position remains strong, leverage low, and maintain a buy rating with a 12‑month target of Rp 29,100 per share and a projected 2026 PBV of 1.01×, while exposure to USD‑denominated financing introduces currency risk.

title: President Commissioner of PT United Tractors Tbk buys 500,000 PT Astra International Tbk shares for Rp2.32 billion
body: Frans Kesuma, President Commissioner of PT United Tractors Tbk and Director of PT Astra International Tbk, bought 500,000 shares of PT Astra International Tbk on 25 June at Rp4,640 per share. The purchase cost Rp2.32 billion, raising his holding in PT Astra International Tbk to 4.3 million shares, or 0,0106% of the company. The transaction occurred less than a month before PT Astra International Tbk’s planned Rp8 trillion share buyback slated for 20 July 2026, which will be voted on at the extraordinary shareholders meeting on 17 July 2026. On Monday 29 June, PT Astra International Tbk’s share price closed at Rp4,710, down 1.05% as the Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.28%, and the stock has dropped 30.74% year‑to‑date.

title: United Tractors' Komatsu sales drop 28.05% in Jan‑May 2026, target cut to 4,000 units
body: United Tractors Tbk reported sales of 1,690 Komatsu heavy‑equipment units from January to May 2026, a 28.05% decline from 2,349 units in the same period of 2025. The sales were led by the mining sector (43% of volume) followed by argo (24%), construction (19%) and forestry (14%). In response, United Tractors revised its 2026 Komatsu sales target to about 4,000 units, down from the original 4,600‑unit goal. The company also lowered other operational targets, including a 15‑17% cut in coal production at PT Pamapersada Nusantara and a coal sales target of 9.6 million tons for 2026 through PT Tuah Turangga Agung.

title: United Tractors announces up to Rp2 trillion share buyback program
body: United Tractors (PT United Tractors Tbk) announced a share repurchase program of up to Rp2 trillion. The buyback is scheduled from 1 July to 30 September 2026 and will be funded entirely from internal resources, not exceeding 20% of the company’s paid‑up capital per POJK No.13/2023. Prior to the new program the company repurchased 35.54 million shares worth Rp860.34 billion, leaving Rp1.13 trillion of the allocated budget still available. United Tractors’ shares rose 1.88% to Rp23,000 after the announcement, while the stock’s price‑to‑book ratio remains at 0.89, well below 1.

title: United Tractors Executes Rp2 Trillion Share Buyback Starting July 1, 2026
body: United Tractors announced the commencement of a share buyback program valued at Rp2 trillion. The program runs from July 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026 and will not exceed 20% of the company's paid‑up capital, while maintaining a free‑float of at least 15%. The company stated that its capital and cash flow are sufficient to fund the buyback without material impact on operations or revenue. United Tractors believes the buyback will reassure investors on fundamental value and help stabilize the stock price amid market volatility. The treasury shares acquired may be sold in the future to raise capital if needed.

title: United Tractors Tbk prepares Rp 2 trillion for share buyback program starting July 2026
body: United Tractors Tbk announced it will allocate up to Rp 2 trillion for a share buyback program running from 1 July to 30 September 2026. The buyback will be funded entirely from internal cash, will not exceed 20% of the company's placed and paid‑up capital, and will keep the free‑float at least 15% of the capital. In the earlier phase (1 April‑30 June 2026) the company repurchased 35,539,100 shares for Rp 860.35 billion, leaving a remaining budget of Rp 1.14 trillion. UNTR may halt the program early if the budget is exhausted or other conditions arise, and the repurchased shares will be held as treasury stock.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk announces up to Rp2 trillion share buyback program through September 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) announced a share buyback program with a maximum allocation of Rp2 trillion. The buyback will be executed from 1 July to 30 September 2026, using internal funds and will not exceed 20 % of the paid‑up capital while keeping the free‑float above the 15 % minimum. Pro forma, the transaction is expected to reduce total assets to about Rp180.5 trillion and equity to Rp99.2 trillion, and lift earnings per share from Rp181 to Rp185. The company said the buyback will not materially affect its operations or cash flow and aligns with government efforts to support market stability.

title: IHSG volatile as BREN, TLKM and BRPT lead gains while United Tractors launches buyback and Erajaya declares dividend
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed in green on July 1, rising 0.92% to 5,695.12 despite overall market volatility. Gains were led by BREN, TLKM and BRPT, while BBRI, BMRI and CPIN weighed on the index, and foreign investors recorded net sales of roughly Rp548 billion in the regular market. PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk announced acceleration of its third nickel rotary‑kiln electric‑furnace project through subsidiary PT Karunia Permai Sentosa, targeting 185,000 t FeNi per year and a total 305,000 t nickel capacity by end‑2026. PT United Tractors Tbk launched a new share‑buyback program of up to Rp2 trillion for July‑September 2026, adding to a prior allocation of Rp2 trillion, while PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk declared a cash dividend of Rp25 per share (≈7.86% yield) and a payout ratio of 32.58% for FY 2025.

title: Technical stock recommendations for Friday, 3 July: PT Astra International Tbk, PT Pakuwon Jati Tbk, and PT United Tractors Tbk
body: The article provides technical trading recommendations for Friday, 3 July for three Indonesian equities. It notes the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 0.87% at 5,744.55 with 20.30 billion shares traded, setting a bullish backdrop. PT Astra International Tbk closed at Rp 4,580, a 0.43% decline, and analysts suggest a “Buy on Weakness” between support Rp 4,470 and resistance Rp 4,790. PT Pakuwon Jati Tbk traded flat at Rp 240, with an “Accumulative Buy” recommendation targeting support Rp 230 and resistance Rp 260, while PT United Tractors Tbk rose 3.52% to Rp 22,800 and is recommended for a “Buy on Break” above Rp 23,000 with target Rp 24,500 and support Rp 21,800.

title: IHSG rebounds to 5,744.55, spotlighting foreign investors' biggest net‑buy stocks
body: Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) closed at 5,744.55 on Thursday, up 49.44 points (0.87%) after a broad sector rally. While foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 237.87 billion across the market, they were net buyers of several individual stocks. The ten stocks with the largest foreign net purchases were PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (Rp 146.0 billion), PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (Rp 94.26 billion), PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp 83.92 billion), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp 75.4 billion), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (Rp 50.85 billion), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (Rp 40.13 billion), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (Rp 19.11 billion), PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (Rp 17.99 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 17.85 billion) and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk (Rp 13.39 billion). These net‑buy figures indicate strong foreign demand for the listed companies despite the overall net outflow.

title: Weekly Top 10 IHSG Supporting Stocks: AMMN, DCII and BREN Lead
body: The article lists the ten stocks that most contributed to the Indonesia Composite Index (IHSG) during the week of 29 June – 3 July 2026. AMMN rose 4.79% and added 9.60 points, DCII gained 4.27% contributing 7.96 points, ANTM up 8.12% adding 4.31 points, IMPC up 10.22% adding 4.22 points, UNTR up 6.19% adding 3.98 points, MPRO up 12.5% adding 3.32 points, ISAT and CUAN up 13.43% and 7.96% adding 2.86 and 2.45 points respectively, BREN up 1.49% adding 2.43 points, and ASII up 1.05% adding 2.26 points. Despite these gains, the IHSG fell 0.35% to 5,875,780 as market capitalization slipped 0.14% to Rp 10,287 trillion and average daily turnover dropped 35.90% to Rp 11.27 trillion. Foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp 6.08 billion for the week, though cumulative net sales since the start of the year total Rp 74.42 trillion.

title: IHSG slides to 5,934 as S&P Dow Jones Indices watchlist pressures market
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) opened lower on Wednesday, 8 July 2026, correcting 51.75 points (‑0.86%) to 5,934.75 after S&P Dow Jones Indices placed Indonesia on its watchlist for a possible downgrade from emerging to frontier market. The decline involved 407 declining stocks versus 144 advancing, with total turnover of 3.8 billion shares worth Rp 1.7 trillion, and ten sector indices traded in the red, led by property (‑1.70%), cyclicals (‑1.64%) and basic materials (‑1.52%). Among large‑cap issuers, PT Solusi Energi Digital Tbk (WIFI) fell 3.46% to Rp 1,675, PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN) dropped 3.09% to Rp 3,450, and PT Semen Indonesia Tbk (SMGR) slipped 2.96% to Rp 1,475, while PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MEDC) rose 3.56% to Rp 1,165, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (TLKM) gained 0.81% to Rp 2,500, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) added 0.52% to Rp 24,125. The watchlist action follows MSCI’s ongoing review of Indonesia’s market status since January 2026, recently extended to November 2026, and coincides with regulator measures raising the free‑float minimum from 7.5% to 15% to improve transparency.

title: IHSG drops 1.11% to 5,920 in morning session, with SMGR, BRPT and CUAN leading losses
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.11% (66.35 points) to 5,920.15 in the first trading session on 8 July 2026. Negative sentiment was sparked after S&P Dow Jones Indices added Indonesia to a watchlist for a possible downgrade from emerging to frontier market status. Among LQ45 constituents, PT Semen Indonesia Tbk declined 3.62% to Rp 1,465, PT Barito Pacific Tbk fell 3.16% to Rp 1,530, and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk dropped 3.15% to Rp 615, while PT Pertamina Geothermal Energy Tbk rose 3.31% to Rp 935, PT AKR Corporindo Tbk gained 2.70% to Rp 1,330, and PT United Tractors Tbk increased 1.67% to Rp 24,400. A total of 447 stocks weakened, 197 strengthened and 142 were unchanged, with trading volume reaching 12.2 billion shares worth Rp 5.2 trillion. The watchlist follows earlier MSCI comments and recent Moody’s and Fitch downgrades of Indonesia’s sovereign rating, which have contributed to net foreign selling of more than US$4 billion this year.

title: LQ45 stocks with the lowest and highest PER on 8 July 2026 saw most shares close lower
body: The article reports that on 8 July 2026 the 20 LQ45 constituents with the lowest and highest price‑earnings ratios mostly closed lower. PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia posted the lowest PER at 3.24 × and fell, while PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi held the highest PER at 200 × and also declined. Among the low‑PER group PT Perusahaan Gas Negara was the only stock to stay positive (+1.42 %), PT Aneka Tambang dropped 4.78 % with the highest trade frequency (22,496 trades) and value (Rp215 billion), and PT Bank Negara Indonesia slipped 2.59 %. In the high‑PER group PT Semen Indonesia recorded the steepest loss of the combined list at –6.58 %, PT United Tractors was the sole gainer (+1.25 %), and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia traded flat at Rp50 despite a volume surge to 281.96 million shares. Overall market turnover reached Rp10.5 trillion and foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp689.8 billion.

title: IHSG Direction Today and Market Stock Picks
body: The Jakarta Stock Exchange (IHSG) opened weaker, down 24.04 points (0.41%) to 5,849 with 3 billion shares traded (Rp1.56 trillion). Broker research highlighted several stocks for the day: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas selected AKRA, ELSA and PGAS; Phintraco Sekuritas chose PGEO, PGAS, UNTR, ITMG and AALI; CGS International Sekuritas Indonesia recommended MEDC, AKRA, ELSA, TLKM, AALI and UNTR; and Panin Sekuritas pointed to BKSL, PGAS and PSAB. The picks reflect expectations amid geopolitical tension, rising oil prices and Indonesia’s inclusion on the S&P Dow Jones watchlist, with analysts noting support levels around 5,800‑5,745 for the index.

title: List of LQ45 stocks with the lowest and highest PER on 9 July 2026, highlighting strong gains in DEWA and BRPT
body: The article presents the July 9 2026 ranking of LQ45 constituents by price‑earnings ratio (PER), noting the stocks with the lowest and highest multiples. DEWA recorded the highest PER (33) and posted the largest price increase of 11.41 % on a volume of 1.22 billion shares, generating a transaction value of about Rp 399.9 billion, while BRPT, with a PER of 1.6, rose 6.67 % and recorded the third‑largest transaction value of Rp 259.5 billion. Other highlighted performers included ANTM (+2.15 % on 19,409 trades), BUMI (volume 2.70 billion shares, transaction value Rp 380.3 billion), INCO (+2 %), GOTO, UNTR, SMGR, MBMA and AMMN, each with their respective PER and PBV figures as listed. The market turned green with total turnover reaching Rp 12.1 trillion and foreign investors’ net selling shrinking to Rp 259.4 billion from Rp 689.8 billion the previous day. The list’s composition changed as PT Merdeka Copper Gold (MDKA) left the top‑PER group and was supplanted by PT Vale Indonesia (INCO).

title: RANS Entertainment Indonesia shares plunge 10.5% as Indonesia Composite Index climbs above 6,000
body: PT Rans Entertainment Indonesia Tbk saw its share price fall 10.53% to Rp204 after an intraday high of Rp282 and low of Rp200, even as the Indonesia Composite Index rose 1.92% to 6,037.84 points on Monday, 13 July 2026. The stock traded 3.4 billion shares with a transaction value of Rp820.6 billion, making it one of the most active securities of the day. Other actively traded companies included PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (up 0.81% to Rp6,225, Rp1.1 trillion traded), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (up 2.87% to Rp2,870, Rp597.1 billion traded), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (up 4.17% to Rp4,250, Rp582.2 billion traded), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (up 8.02% to Rp1,750), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (up 7.69% to Rp3,780) and PT United Tractors Tbk (up 5.71% to Rp25,900). PT Rans Entertainment Indonesia Tbk is controlled by Raffi Ahmad and Nagita Slavina, and the market rally occurred on the 34th anniversary of the Indonesia Stock Exchange.

title: Indo Premier Sekuritas raises automotive sector recommendation to Overweight ahead of GIIAS
body: Indo Premier Sekuritas upgraded its recommendation for the Indonesian automotive sector to Overweight ahead of the Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS). The broker pointed to a 12% month‑on‑month rise in national four‑wheel wholesale volume to about 77,600 units in June 2026, driven by strong sales of BYD, Mitsubishi, Daihatsu and Wuling, and a 4% increase for PT Astra International Tbk to 40,200 units, highlighted by a 26% jump in Daihatsu’s Gran Max model. BYD’s electric‑vehicle sales surged 284% month‑on‑month, contributing to a 32% rise in total xEV sales to 23,000 units, while PT United Tractors Tbk, a subsidiary of PT Astra International Tbk, is expected to benefit from relaxed coal‑budget regulations. Indo Premier noted that the sector’s valuation appears more attractive after a sharp correction in ASII’s share price, though it warned of regulatory risks.

title: PT Astra International Tbk’s car sales rise 10% YoY, analyst recommends buying the stock
body: The article discusses the outlook for PT Astra International Tbk’s automotive segment, noting a 10% year‑on‑year increase in car sales to 222,371 units in the first half of 2026. This growth kept Astra’s domestic market share above 50% while national car sales grew 16% to 436,567 units, and the analyst highlighted spill‑over benefits to its financing, insurance, components and after‑sales businesses. However, the analyst warned that slower growth relative to the market, competition from electric and hybrid manufacturers, high interest rates, and weaker contributions from United Tractors’ heavy‑equipment and mining operations could moderate profit expansion. The recommendation is a buy (or buy on weakness) with technical targets of breaking the Rp5,000 resistance and moving toward Rp5,400‑Rp5,600, and ultimately Rp6,000‑Rp6,100 per share.

title: Astra International's stock outlook stays positive, supported by automotive market recovery
body: The article assesses the outlook for PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) through 2026, concluding the stock remains positive thanks to the ongoing recovery of Indonesia’s automotive market. Astra’s H1‑2026 vehicle sales rose 10% YoY to 222,371 units, preserving a market share above 50% despite the national market growing 16% YoY to 436,567 units. The analyst notes that while the automotive recovery and strong financing, insurance and after‑sales businesses support growth, weaker commodity prices and the performance of the heavy‑equipment subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk pose downside risks. Technically, the stock faces resistance at Rp5,000 with upside targets of Rp5,400‑5,600 and a further goal of Rp6,000‑6,100 if volume backs a breakout.

title: Analyst projects continued positive performance for PT Astra International Tbk to 2026 and issues a buy‑on‑weakness recommendation
body: The article discusses an analyst’s outlook that PT Astra International Tbk will maintain a positive performance trajectory through the end of 2026. It cites first‑half‑2026 vehicle sales of 222,371 units, a 10 % year‑on‑year increase, while the national market grew 16 % to 436,567 units, allowing Astra to keep a market share above 50 %. The analyst notes that Astra’s integrated businesses—including financing, insurance, components, after‑sales services and its heavy‑equipment arm United Tractors—provide cross‑segment support, though higher interest rates, a weaker rupiah and competitive pressure from electric and hybrid vehicles pose risks. Technically, the stock faces resistance at Rp 5,000 and, if broken with strong volume, the target range is Rp 5,400‑5,600 with a longer‑term aim of Rp 6,000‑6,100. The analyst recommends a buy‑on‑weakness strategy for ASII shares.

title: LQ45 stocks on 14 July 2026 show lowest and highest PERs, with Barito Pacific and United Tractors highlighted
body: The article lists LQ45 constituents with the lowest price‑to‑earnings ratios and the highest performers on 14 July 2026, emphasizing Barito Pacific (BRPT) and United Tractors (UNTR). Total market turnover rose to Rp16.8 trillion, while foreign investors bought 601.6 million shares but sold Rp830.3 billion in value. BRPT and Amman Mineral Internasional each corrected by about 3.4 % but BRPT recorded the largest transaction value at Rp578.6 billion; UNTR surged 6.18 % to lead the group, with Vale Indonesia up 4.01 % and Hartadinata Abadi gaining 3.95 %. Semen Indonesia held the cheapest PBV at 0.22× (Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper 0.34×), while Bumi Resources posted the highest share volume at 3.46 billion shares despite a transaction value of Rp520.1 billion; Perusahaan Gas Negara fell 2.61 %.

title: UBS Sekuritas dominates buying and selling activity among blue‑chip stocks on 17 July 2026
body: The article reports broker activity for Indonesia's blue‑chip stocks on 17 July 2026, highlighting UBS Sekuritas. Foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp638.0 billion in value while net selling volume reached 459.9 million shares, and total market turnover was Rp16.3 trillion. UBS Sekuritas was the largest buyer for BBCA (50.5 million shares, Rp322.3 billion), TLKM (40.4 million shares, Rp106.4 billion), BBNI (13.5 million shares, Rp48.4 billion) and UNTR (1.1 million shares, Rp28.4 billion), and also the top seller for BBCA and ICBP, appearing in six of the twenty broker‑stock rows. Other brokers such as Mandiri Sekuritas (buyer for AMMN and ICBP) and Maybank Sekuritas (seller for AMMN and BBNI) were mentioned, covering the full set of blue‑chip companies BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, AMMN, TLKM, ASII, BRPT, BBNI, UNTR and ICBP.

title: Technical buy and hold recommendations for BREN, ACES, and UNTR ahead of Thursday trading (23 July)
body: The article provides technical trading recommendations for PT Barito Renewables Energy Tbk (BREN), PT Aspirasi Hidup Indonesia Tbk (ACES) and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) for Thursday 23 July 2026. BREN closed up 6.0% at Rp 3,710 on Wednesday, with analysts noting a three‑white‑soldiers pattern, rising RSI and volume, and setting support at Rp 3,360 and resistance at Rp 3,760, prompting a buy recommendation. ACES traded flat at Rp 358, showing bullish consolidation supported by positive Stochastics K_D and RSI, with support Rp 340, resistance Rp 364, and a maintain‑buy stance. UNTR fell 2.11% to Rp 25,550, expected to correct minorly before testing resistance near Rp 27,975 if it stays above Rp 25,150, leading to a hold recommendation with support Rp 25,150 and resistance Rp 27,950.

title: Stock Recommendations and IHSG Movement for 23 July 2026
body: The article provides a daily market commentary on the Jakarta Stock Exchange, noting that the IHSG index closed at 6,334.48 on 21 July 2026, down 0.09%. It reports price declines for LQ45 constituents PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (down 3.26% to Rp4,150), PT United Tractors Tbk (down 2.11% to Rp25,550), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (down 2.04% to Rp720), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (down 2.01% to Rp730), PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk (down 1.82% to Rp540), and PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (down 1.82% to Rp2,700). It highlights gains for PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (up 3.86% to Rp2,020), PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (up 3.53% to Rp1,320), and PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (up 2.56% to Rp3,210). MNC Sekuritas recommends buying on weakness PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk, PT Bukit Asam Tbk, and a trading buy for PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk, while projecting IHSG support at 6,111–5,839 and resistance at 6,377–6,599.

title: Top 10 weekly laggards, led by BMRI, BBCA and ASII, weigh on Indonesia's IHSG
body: The article lists the ten stocks that most dragged down the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) during the week of 20‑24 July 2026. Bank Mandiri (BMRI) led the list, falling 7.81% and pulling the index down by 28.57 points, followed by Bank Central Asia (BBCA) down 3.09% contributing 17.65 points and Astra International (ASII) down 2.35% adding 4.89 points. Additional contributors were DCII (owned by Toto Sugiri) with 3.35 points, United Tractors (UNTR) 3.11 points, Mitra Sinerji (MSIN) 2.80 points, Telekomunikasi Indonesia (TLKM) 2.77 points, Film (FILM) 2.37 points, XL Axiata (EXCL) 2.17 points and BUVA (affiliated with Happy Hapsoro) 2.07 points. Despite these pressures, the IHSG closed the week up 0.34% at 6,196,430, while trading volume and value rose sharply and foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.36 trillion on the final day.

title: Indo Premier Sekuritas forecasts PT Astra International core net profit of Rp13.5 trillion for H1 2026
body: Indo Premier Sekuritas projects PT Astra International Tbk.'s core net profit to reach Rp13.5 trillion in the first half of 2026. The forecast rests on a 19% quarter‑on‑quarter rise in wholesale automotive sales to 222,000 units and strong results from its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk., which is expected to deliver Rp3.5 trillion core profit for the same period after a Rp2 trillion Q2 profit. Additional contributions are anticipated from PT Astra Otoparts Tbk. and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk., with AALI projected to post roughly Rp1.1 trillion core profit in H1 2026. IPOT maintains a buy‑back recommendation, citing the shareholder‑approved Rp8 trillion share repurchase on 17 July 2026 as a positive catalyst for the stock.

title: United Tractors posts 15% lower H1 2026 revenue and 88% plunge in profit attributable to shareholders
body: The article reports United Tractors' (UNTR) financial performance for the first half of 2026, showing a significant deterioration. Consolidated net revenue fell 15% year‑on‑year to Rp58.3 trillion from Rp68.52 trillion. Net profit excluding non‑recurring items dropped 48% to Rp4.3 trillion, and profit attributable to the parent shareholders plunged 88% to Rp956 billion, driven mainly by lower gold sales from Agincourt Resources and weaker heavy‑equipment and coal‑mining segments. The company recorded non‑recurring losses of Rp3.3 trillion, net debt of Rp9.4 trillion with a gearing ratio of 8.5%, and noted that the temporary shutdown of the Martabe Gold Mine was lifted in Q2. UNTR attributed part of the offsetting revenue to higher mining‑contractor income supported by a stronger US dollar and highlighted ongoing gold‑mining acquisitions and a share‑buyback program.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk net profit drops 88% in first half of 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk reported that its net profit fell 88.2% to Rp956.28 billion in the first half of 2026 compared with Rp8.13 trillion a year earlier. Revenue declined 15% to Rp58.29 trillion, driven by lower gold sales at PT Agincourt Resources and weaker performance in the heavy‑equipment and coal‑mining segments, with Komatsu equipment sales down 27% to 1,994 units. Operating cash flow dropped to Rp2.75 trillion and investing cash outflow rose to Rp12.39 trillion as the company pursued acquisitions of a gold‑mining subsidiary and a share‑buyback program, leaving net debt at Rp9.4 trillion and a gearing ratio of 8.5%. Despite the profit slump, the mining‑contractor business posted a 4% revenue increase to Rp27.2 trillion, helped by a stronger US dollar.

title: United Tractors (UNTR) reports revenue of Rp58.3 trillion for the first half of 2026
body: United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), an issuer of the Astra Group, posted first‑half 2026 revenue of Rp58.3 trillion, 15 % lower than the same period a year earlier. Net profit after tax fell to Rp956 billion, an 88 % decline, while profit excluding non‑recurring items dropped 48 % to Rp4.3 trillion. The downturn was driven by weaker gold sales at PT Agincourt Resources and the temporary shutdown of Tambang Emas Martabe, as well as reduced coal volumes from the national RKAB allocation affecting the thermal and metallurgical coal mining segment operated by PT Tuah Turangga Agung and lower heavy‑equipment sales; however, the mining‑contractor segment run through PAMA Group saw a 4 % revenue increase to Rp27.2 trillion helped by a stronger US dollar. As of 30 June 2026 the company’s net debt rose to Rp9.4 trillion (gearing 8.5 %) against cash of Rp7.7 trillion at 31 December 2025, reflecting recent gold‑mine acquisition and a share‑buyback program.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk reports 15% revenue decline and 48% net profit drop in H1 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk said its consolidated net revenue fell 15% year‑on‑year to Rp 58.3 trillion in the first half of 2026, while net profit (excluding non‑recurring items) dropped 48% to Rp 4.3 trillion. The decline was driven by lower gold sales from PT Agincourt Resources and reduced performance in the heavy‑equipment and thermal‑and‑metallurgical coal segments, reflecting a weaker national RKAB coal allocation. Offsetting contributions came from the mining‑contractor unit run by PT Pamapersada Nusantara and its subsidiary PT Kalimantan Prima Persada, which posted a 4% increase in revenue to Rp 27.2 trillion, and from a stronger US dollar, while the coal‑mining unit operated by PT Tuah Turangga Agung saw revenue fall 4% to Rp 12.9 trillion and the gold‑and‑other‑minerals unit, run by PT Agincourt Resources, PT Sumbawa Jutaraya, PT Stargate Pasific Resources and the 20.13%‑owned Nickel Industries Limited, recorded a 66% revenue drop to Rp 2.4 trillion. As of 30 June 2026 the company held net debt of Rp 9.4 trillion (gearing 8.5%) and cash of Rp 7.7 trillion, with non‑recurring items amounting to Rp 3.3 trillion.

title: United Tractors posts 48% YoY decline in H1 2026 net profit as revenue falls 15%
body: United Tractors (UNTR) released its H1 2026 financial results showing a sharp contraction in profitability. Net profit excluding non‑recurring items fell 48% year‑on‑year to Rp4.3 trillion while revenue dropped 15% to Rp58.3 trillion, driven by weaker gold sales from PT Agincourt Resources and lower coal allocation. The heavy‑equipment segment saw revenue fall 28% to Rp15 trillion as unit sales slipped 27% to 1,994, whereas the mining‑contractor segment, represented by subsidiaries PT Pamapersada Nusantara and PT Kalimantan Prima Persada, grew 4% to Rp27.2 trillion. Net debt rose to Rp9.4 trillion (gearing 8.5%) and the company continued its share‑buyback program, authorising up to Rp2 trillion of repurchases through 30 Sept 2026, having bought back 237 million shares worth Rp7.1 trillion since 2022.

title: United Tractors reports Rp58.3 trillion revenue for H1 2026, down 15% YoY
body: United Tractors, a subsidiary of PT Astra International Tbk, posted net revenue of Rp58.3 trillion in the first half of 2026, a 15% year‑on‑year decline from Rp68.5 trillion. The decline was driven by lower gold sales from its subsidiary PT Agincourt Resources after a temporary shutdown of the Martabe gold mine and weaker performance in the heavy‑equipment and thermal‑coal mining segments due to reduced national coal allocation. Net profit excluding non‑recurring items fell 48% to Rp4.3 trillion, while non‑recurring losses totaled Rp3.3 trillion, and net debt rose to Rp9.4 trillion, giving a gearing ratio of 8.5% as of 30 June 2026. Heavy‑equipment revenue fell 28% to Rp15.0 trillion as Komatsu equipment sales slipped 27% to 1,994 units, though parts and service revenue edged up to Rp5.5 trillion. The company noted that a stronger US‑dollar exchange rate and a share‑buyback programme partially offset the revenue shortfall.

title: United Tractors' Net Profit Plummets 88% as 2026 RKAB Coal Allocation Cuts Hit Sales
body: United Tractors Tbk said the reduction in the 2026 mining work plan and budget (RKAB) allocation for coal was a key factor pressuring its first‑half 2026 performance. Net profit fell 88.2% year‑on‑year to Rp956.28 billion and revenue dropped 15% to Rp58.29 trillion. Sales of Komatsu construction equipment fell 27% to 1,994 units, coal segment revenue slipped 4% to Rp12.9 trillion, and gold‑related revenue collapsed 66% to Rp2.4 trillion after the Martabe gold mine was offline, while mining contractor services rose 4% to Rp27.2 trillion aided by a weaker rupiah. The company hopes the government will increase RKAB allocation in the second half of 2026, which it expects could revive demand for heavy equipment, coal, and mining services.

title: PT Astra International Tbk reports H1 2026 revenue of Rp 157.9 trillion and net profit of Rp 12.5 trillion
body: PT Astra International Tbk posted consolidated net revenue of Rp 157.9 trillion and net profit of Rp 12.5 trillion for the first half of 2026. Revenue fell 3% YoY and net profit declined 19% while adjusted net profit (excluding non‑recurring items) dropped 7% to Rp 14.9 trillion, with Rp 2.4 trillion of non‑recurring items mainly fair‑value adjustments and impairment. The lower contribution from the mining solutions and heavy‑equipment business was offset by gains in automotive and financial‑services segments, and net debt rose to Rp 6 trillion (excluding financial‑services subsidiaries) as the group completed the acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam and executed share‑buyback and working‑capital actions. PT Astra International Tbk approved a new share‑buyback program of up to Rp 8 trillion for the next 12 months, and United Tractors announced its own buyback of up to Rp 2 trillion for three months, adding to the combined Rp 7.4 trillion buyback completed through June 2026. The company reaffirmed its new corporate strategy focused on automotive, financial services, and mining‑solution businesses amid ongoing global uncertainty.

title: Astra International posts Rp12.53 trillion net profit in H1 2026, announces up‑to‑Rp8 trillion share buyback
body: Astra International Tbk reported net profit of Rp12.53 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 19 % decline year‑on‑year, with earnings per share falling to Rp313. Consolidated revenue slipped 3 % to Rp157.91 trillion, while adjusted profit excluding non‑recurring items was Rp14.89 trillion, down 7 % YoY. Profit fell mainly in the mining solutions and heavy‑equipment segment, which posted Rp2.70 trillion versus Rp5.02 trillion a year earlier, whereas automotive, financial‑services and other businesses posted gains of 9 %, 6 % and 31 % respectively. The company unveiled a new corporate strategy focused on automotive, financial services and mining solutions, and announced a share‑buyback programme of up to Rp8 trillion for the next 12 months, while its subsidiary United Tractors Tbk launched a separate buyback of up to Rp2 trillion for three months.

title: Astra International posts half‑year profit of Rp12.5 trillion and announces up to Rp8 trillion share buyback
body: Astra International reported half‑year 2026 net profit of Rp12.5 trillion, backed by consolidated revenue of Rp157.9 trillion. The group saw automotive earnings rise 9% YoY, financial services up 6% YoY and other businesses jump 81% YoY, while contributions from mining solutions and heavy equipment fell, pressuring overall profit. Astra approved a new share buyback program of up to Rp8 trillion over the next 12 months at the extraordinary shareholders meeting on 17 July 2026, and its subsidiary United Tractors announced a Rp2 trillion buyback for three months. United Tractors posted an 88.2% decline in net profit to Rp956.28 billion and a 15% revenue drop to Rp58.29 trillion, citing weaker gold sales from PT Agincourt Resources and reduced coal mining activity under the 2026 national RKAB. Stockbit analysts project Astra’s full‑year 2026 net profit could reach around Rp29 trillion if no further one‑off charges arise.

title: United Tractors' Net Profit Falls 48% in H1 2026 as Coal RKAB Allocation and Gold Sales Decline
body: United Tractors Tbk reported a net profit of Rp 4.3 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 48 % decline from Rp 8.2 trillion a year earlier. The drop was driven by a 15 % fall in net revenue to Rp 58.3 trillion, reflecting weaker gold sales from Tambang Emas Martabe, which is managed by PT Agincourt Resources, and a lower national RKAB coal allocation. Equipment sales also weakened, with Komatsu units down 27 % to 1,994 and large‑size units down 55 % to 325, causing the equipment segment revenue to fall 28 % to Rp 15 trillion. However, the mining contractor segment operated by PT Pamapersada Nusantara and PT Kalimantan Prima Persada posted a 4 % revenue increase to Rp 27.2 trillion, while the coal mining segment run by PT Tuah Turangga Agung saw volume and revenue declines of 10 % and 4 % respectively.

title: JP Morgan recommends accumulation of PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) citing strong automotive earnings despite a 26% profit decline.
body: JP Morgan calls for investors to accumulate PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) after noting resilient automotive earnings. The bank reports ASII’s net profit fell 26% year‑on‑year to Rp6.7 trillion in Q2 2026, with first‑half profit down 22% to Rp12.5 trillion. Excluding the weaker performance of UNTR, JP Morgan estimates a core profit of Rp8 trillion, above the consensus of Rp7.3 trillion. The automotive segment posted a 19% rise in net profit to Rp3.5 trillion, and PT Astra Daihatsu Motor’s manufacturing margin improved to 7% from 5.5% a year earlier.

title: Astra International posts 22% YoY profit decline in Q2 2026, analysts keep buy recommendation
body: PT Astra International Tbk reported net profit of Rp 6.7 trillion in Q2 2026, 22.1% lower YoY and only 39.7% of MNC Sekuritas estimate, indicating performance below expectations. The decline was driven by a Rp 2.4 trillion non‑recurring charge from fair‑value adjustments and impairments in its geothermal and nickel divisions, while the mining solutions segment saw revenue fall 15% YoY and mining profit plunge 88% YoY to Rp 607 billion. Despite the weakness, the automotive and financial services segments grew about 6% YoY, with automotive sales gaining a 51% market share, and the group’s cash‑rich position supported a continued buyback program. Analysts from BRI Danareksa and MNC Sekuritas kept a buy rating on PT Astra International Tbk, setting target prices of Rp 6,850 and Rp 7,000 respectively, and highlighted the subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk as the main weight on earnings but with potential recovery in the second half of 2026.

title: ASII profit projected to rebound in H2 2026 with target net profit up to Rp29 trillion, analysts say
body: PT Astra International Tbk posted a Q2 2026 net profit of Rp 6.7 trillion, 22 % lower YoY but 14 % higher QoQ, representing about 43 % of the consensus 2026 profit forecast of Rp 29 trillion. Stockbit Investment analysts expect the second‑half of 2026 to lift Astra’s annual net profit to the Rp 28‑29 trillion range, citing the absence of further one‑off charges, possible RKAB revisions and a recovery in gold output at the Martabe mine that should boost its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk. Kiwoom Sekuritas analyst Adrian Djie, however, flags pressure from the Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy segment and a Rp 3.3 trillion one‑off charge at UNTR, noting that UNTR’s earnings remain under strain. Both analysts maintain buy recommendations, setting target prices of Rp 6,400 for Astra and Rp 29,100 for United Tractors, while United Tractors’s price‑to‑book ratio is near minus‑two standard deviations of its five‑year average.

title: Foreign investors net sold Rp 250.53 billion over the weekend, with PT MNC Digital Entertainment Tbk leading the top‑10 most‑sold stocks
body: Foreign investors posted a net sell of Rp 250.53 billion in Indonesia’s equity market on Friday 31 July 2026, even as the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 0.80% at 6,236.12 points. The market saw a trading volume of 32.06 billion shares worth Rp 17.96 trillion, with 437 stocks advancing, 193 declining and 159 unchanged. The ten stocks most heavily sold by foreigners were PT MNC Digital Entertainment Tbk (Rp 160.48 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 106.42 billion), PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (Rp 100.4 billion), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (Rp 72.4 billion), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (Rp 71.73 billion), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp 33.82 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 29.3 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 22.69 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp 19.02 billion) and PT Indosat Tbk (Rp 18.25 billion). Sector gains were led by basic materials (+2.54%) and health care (+2.43%), indicating broader market strength despite the foreign outflow.

title: Popular financial news roundup covers Antam gold price outlook, UNTR losses and discounts, IHSG prospects, and BMRI valuation
body: The article presents a roundup of the five most popular financial news items for the week ending 2 August 2026, focusing on Antam’s gold price outlook, the IHSG outlook with six leading stocks, United Tractors’ sharp profit decline, jewelry gold price stability, and Bank Mandiri’s discounted valuation. PT Antam Tbk’s gold price was reported at Rp 2,603 000 per gram on 1 August 2026 with analysts projecting further weakness at the support level, while PT United Tractors Tbk posted a Q2‑2026 net loss of Rp 314 billion, bringing semester‑I profit to Rp 956 billion after a large impairment on geothermal assets linked to PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap. The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 10.28 % in July 2026 and is expected to continue strengthening in August, driven by six stocks—BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, INCO, ANTM, and TLKM—though market direction may be affected by upcoming BI governor changes and US labor data. Bank Mandiri’s solid first‑half performance supports a buy recommendation with a 12‑month target price implying a projected 2026 price‑to‑book ratio of 1.5 times, above the three‑year average of 1.35 times.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk records Rp2.7 trillion impairment on geothermal investment in PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dadap
body: PT United Tractors Tbk reported a Rp2.76 trillion impairment on its investment in PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dadap, writing the investment down to zero and recognizing a Rp1.47 trillion loss on the asset and a Rp1.28 trillion loss on related non‑operating receivables. The impairment contributed to a sharp decline in first‑half 2026 net profit to Rp956.28 billion, an 88.2 % drop year‑over‑year, while total revenue fell 15 % to Rp58.29 trillion. UNTR, an affiliate of Grup Astra, holds a 40.4 % stake in SERD through PT Energia Prima Nusantara and PT Pamapersada Nusantara, and SERD, a subsidiary of PT Supreme Energy, operates a 2 × 49 MW geothermal plant with a potential expansion to 2 × 110 MW under a Power Purchase Agreement with PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara. The company’s balance sheet showed assets of Rp179.06 trillion, liabilities of Rp77.31 trillion, equity of Rp101.75 trillion, cash of Rp18.65 trillion, operating cash flow of Rp2.75 trillion and a net‑debt‑to‑equity gearing of 8.5 %.

title: Majority of LQ45 Index constituents post solid performance in H1 2026
body: The majority of LQ45 Index constituents delivered solid financial results in the first half of 2026. PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) posted the highest net‑profit growth at 919.58% YoY to US$19.78 million, followed by PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) with 354% YoY and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (INCO) with 313.4% YoY. Six constituents—PT Astra International Tbk (ASII), PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP), PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF), PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (KLBF)—recorded lower net profit, while banks BBCA, BMRI and BBTN posted net profits of roughly IDR 29.5 trillion, IDR 30.4 trillion and a 41% YoY increase respectively. Equity research analyst Alrich Paskalis highlighted continued credit growth and commodity‑price support and issued buy recommendations on BMRI, BBCA, AMRT, CPIN and KLBF with target prices of IDR 4,900, 7,000, 1,500‑1,600, 4,000 and 1,000 per share.

title: Analyst highlights strong first‑half 2026 earnings across LQ45 constituents and points to several stocks with upside potential through year‑end 2026
body: The analyst notes that most LQ45 constituents posted solid first‑half 2026 earnings, exceeding market expectations. PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk posted the highest YoY net profit growth at 919.58% to US$19.78 million, followed by PT Indika Energy Tbk (354%) and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (313.4%). Six constituents—PT Astra International Tbk, PT United Tractors Tbk, PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk, PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk, and PT Kalbe Farma Tbk—recorded profit declines. Strong performance also came from CPIN (95.1% YoY to Rp 3.7 trillion), UNVR (37.7% YoY to Rp 2.97 trillion), MAPI (26.49% YoY to Rp 1.21 trillion), GOTO (net profit Rp 607.48 billion), ISAT (84.5% YoY to Rp 4.3 trillion), BMRI (24.4% YoY to Rp 30.4 trillion) and INCO, NCKL, HRTA with notable gains. The analyst projects that these and other LQ45 stocks remain attractive through the end of 2026, supported by domestic consumption recovery and anticipated monetary easing.

title: Prospects and Recommendations for LQ45 Constituents After First‑Half 2026 Earnings
body: The article reviews the earnings released by LQ45 constituents for the first half of 2026 and evaluates their stock prospects. Of the 29 companies that have reported, most posted revenue and profit growth, while six showed profit declines, with banking stocks BMRI and BBCA highlighted for solid performance—BMRI posted a 24.4% YoY profit increase and BBCA maintained stable earnings and a credit portfolio exceeding Rp1 trillion. Conversely, ICBP’s profit fell 33% due to currency losses and UNTR faced operational pressure; consumer‑goods firm UNVR’s gross profit margin slipped to 44.9% in Q2 2026, and automotive group ASII reported net profit of Rp6.7 trillion, down 22.14% YoY. Analysts from Kiwoom Securities and Ajaib Securities note that despite a positive overall outlook for LQ45, selective strength and macro‑headwinds such as a 100‑basis‑point rate hike to 5.75% and a PMI contraction to 46.9 keep the outlook mixed.

title: LQ45 constituents post solid first‑half 2026 earnings, with top blue‑chip picks highlighted for semester II
body: The article reports that the majority of LQ45 index constituents delivered first‑half 2026 net‑profit results that beat market expectations. PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk posted the highest YoY profit growth at 919.58% to US$19.78 million, followed by PT Indika Energy Tbk (354%) and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk (313.4%); PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk, PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk, PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk, PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, PT Indosat Tbk and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk also recorded strong gains ranging from 24.4% to 95.1% YoY, while PT Trimegah Bangun Persada Tbk and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk contributed to the mining sector rebound. Six constituents – PT Astra International Tbk, PT United Tractors Tbk, PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk, PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk and PT Kalbe Farma Tbk – posted declines in net profit. Analyst Elandry Pratama of Panin Sekuritas highlighted the solid performance of consumer, technology, telecom and banking stocks and projected that BMRI, ISAT, CPIN, INCO and GOTO remain attractive for the second semester, supported by domestic consumption recovery, post‑merger synergies and potential foreign inflows. The outlook also notes that a possible interest‑rate cut in the second half of 2026 could further boost the broader LQ45 sector.

title: Indonesia's IHSG jumps 1.37% as foreign investors net buy Rp623 billion, led by major banks
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 1.37% at 6,319.61 points on 4 August 2026, driven by strong foreign buying. Foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp623.48 billion across the market, with net buying of Rp741.19 billion in the regular market and a net sell of Rp117.71 billion in the cash‑negotiated segment, accounting for 32.90% of total transaction value. The top net‑foreign‑buy stocks were PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (Rp404.43 billion), PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (Rp129.87 billion), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (Rp116.06 billion) and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (Rp94.05 billion), all of which posted price gains of 3.17% to 3.98% during the session. Other gainers included PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia Tbk, PT Astra International Tbk and PT United Tractors Tbk, which rose between 0.84% and 1.82%.

title: Technical trading recommendations for AKRA, TAPG, and UNTR for Wednesday, 5 August 2026
body: The article provides technical trading recommendations for three Indonesian stocks—PT AKR Corporindo Tbk (AKRA), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (TAPG) and PT United Tractors (UNTR)—for the session on Wednesday, 5 August 2026. It notes that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 1.37% at 6,319.61 on Tuesday, with a total turnover of 32.96 billion shares and Rp 12.75 trillion in value, setting a bullish backdrop. For AKRA, analysts recommend buying on weakness within the Rp 1,400–1,420 support zone, with a stop‑loss below Rp 1,380 and a target of Rp 1,490 after the stock closed at Rp 1,450, up 0.35% on Tuesday. TAPG is advised to buy on weakness between Rp 1,740–1,750, targeting Rp 1,910 after closing at Rp 1,820, down 1.09% with RSI in overbought territory, while UNTR is suggested for speculative buying at support Rp 23,525, aiming for Rp 24,900 after a close at Rp 24,000, up 0.84% supported by a bullish harami pattern and oversold RSI.

title: Indo Premier Sekuritas raises profit forecasts and lifts price target to Rp 5,900 for PT Astra International Tbk (ASII)
body: Indo Premier Sekuritas upgraded its outlook for PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) after strong first‑half 2026 results. It increased core profit estimates for 2026‑2028 by 2‑10% and raised the target price to Rp 5,900 from Rp 5,800, while the stock closed down 1.95% at Rp 5,025 per share. The revision is driven by better performance of automotive subsidiaries PT Astra Daihatsu Motor (ADM) and PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO), with ADM margin raised to 6% and its profit projection up 19%, and an expected 20% annual growth in joint‑venture revenue. Indo Premier also lifted core‑profit forecasts for other ASII subsidiaries, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) (+4‑53%) and PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) (+3‑8%). Revenue and net‑profit targets for ASII in 2026 were revised upward to Rp 329.72 trillion and Rp 30.42 trillion, and vehicle wholesale volume is projected at 900,000 units, assuming ASII retains a 50% market share.

title: Assessing Conglomerate Stock Prospects After First‑Half 2026 Performance
body: The article evaluates the outlook of Indonesian conglomerate‑listed stocks following their first‑half 2026 results. PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk reported revenue of Rp 65.53 trillion (+9% YoY) but net profit fell 19% to Rp 4.72 trillion; PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk saw sales rise 16% YoY with net profit up 25% YoY; PT Barito Pacific Tbk posted a 71.6% revenue increase to US$5.69 billion while net profit dropped 64.8% to US$190 million; and PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk grew revenue 22.7% YoY to Rp 10.81 trillion yet recorded a loss of Rp 4.23 trillion. Other highlighted conglomerates include DCII, TOWR, BREN, AALI, SCMA, CUAN, DMAS, SUPA, BUMI, ICBP, ROTI, IMAS, ASII, UNTR, BSDE, BUKA, AUTO, BBCA, SRTG and TPIA, with analysts pointing to data‑center and digital‑infrastructure firms (DCII, TOWR), renewable‑energy player BREN, and plantation companies AALI and LSIP as having the strongest growth potential. Kiwoom Securities’ Liza Camelia Suryanata and Pilarmas Investindo’s Maximilianus Nico Demus each issued target‑price recommendations, notably ASII at Rp 6,580, INDF at Rp 8,420, ICBP at Rp 9,760, SRTG at Rp 2,850, BBCA at Rp 8,130 (Liza’s 12‑month target Rp 8,075), AUTO at Rp 3,270 and TPIA at Rp 3,190 per share. The analysts caution that margin pressure, funding costs, commodity‑price volatility and limited free‑float valuations could temper upside, but they expect conglomerates’ diversified business models to sustain resilience through 2026.

title: United Tractors (UNTR) Outlook Remains Pressured as H1 2026 Profit Falls 88% and Recovery Hinges on RKAB Revision and Martabe Mine Restart
body: United Tractors (UNTR) posted a sharp 88.2% YoY decline in first‑half 2026 net profit to Rp 956.28 billion as revenue fell 15% YoY to Rp 58.29 trillion, keeping the company under pressure. Analysts attribute the drop to lower gold sales from PT Agincourt Resources and weaker performance in heavy‑equipment and thermal‑metalurgical coal segments after a reduced national RKAB allocation for 2026. The firm’s 2026 outlook depends on a possible July RKAB revision that could revive equipment demand and on the resumption of the Martabe gold mine, with projected gold output of 60 k oz in 2026 and 80‑100 k oz in 2027. Despite the challenges, broker target prices range from Rp 22,600 to Rp 31,500 per share, reflecting divergent views on the recovery potential.

title: UNTR's Net Profit Falls 88% YoY to Rp 956.28bn, Analysts Cite Diversification and Gold Prices as Potential Support
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) reported an 88.2% year‑on‑year decline in net profit to Rp 956.28 billion for the first half of 2026, with revenue falling 15% to Rp 58.29 trillion. Analysts from Mirae Asset Sekuritas, OCBC Sekuritas and Sucor Sekuritas said the drop reflects weaker coal RKAB allocations, reduced mining contribution and the temporary shutdown of the Martabe gold mine, but highlighted the company's diversified business lines and a possible rebound in gold prices as mitigating factors. Forecasts project UNTR’s 2026 revenue to decline 18.8% YoY to Rp 106.63 trillion and net profit to shrink 32% YoY to about Rp 10.07 trillion, with target prices of Rp 22,600 (hold) and Rp 29,000 (buy) issued by the two brokerages. Risks noted include tighter government RKAB policies, lower global coal prices, exchange‑rate volatility and delays in normalising Martabe operations, while a planned tailings‑storage facility slated for Q3 2027 aims to support future gold output of 80‑100 k oz in 2027 and 200 k oz in 2028.

title: Stock Recommendations and IHSG Movement for August 11, 2026
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) slipped 0.69% to 6,365.37 on August 11, 2026, trading between 6,462.74 and 6,362.76. Among LQ45 constituents, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk, PT Barito Pacific Tbk, PT Indika Energy Tbk, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk, PT Indosat Tbk and PT Elang Mahkota Teknologi Tbk led declines of 3‑4%, while PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk, PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk, PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk, PT United Tractors Tbk, PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk and PT Bukit Asam Tbk posted gains ranging from 0.8% to 7.9%. MNC Sekuritas recommended buying on weakness PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT ESSA Industries Indonesia Tbk and PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk, and a trading‑buy position for PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk. The broker highlighted support at 6,319‑6,201 and resistance at 6,454‑6,599, indicating limited upside pending macro developments.

title: Analysts deem mining‑services issuers still prospective and highlight UNTR, DEWA, MYOH as top picks
body: The article discusses analysts’ view that mining‑services companies remain promising through 2026 despite a dip in Indonesia’s coal export volume. BPS data show coal export value of US$12.04 billion in Jan‑Jun 2026 (+0.63% YoY) while volume fell 6.37% to 184.20 million tons, and the producer‑price index rose 8.03% QoQ, indicating price support. Equity analyst Imam Gunadi and Infovesta analyst Ekky Topan note that contractor performance depends more on client production, stripping ratio, equipment utilisation and coal price than on export volume, and cite the 10% overburden‑volume decline at PT Pamapersada Nusantara, a subsidiary of PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR). Based on this outlook, they recommend buying UNTR with a target of Rp 27,700‑30,000 (Imam holds at Rp 28,500), DEWA with a target of Rp 670‑700, and consider MYOH attractive, while DOID is kept on a wait‑and‑see basis. The analysts also stress diversification into other minerals and EPC projects to mitigate risks from RKAB policy tightening.

title: IHSG up 1.69% on Aug 13, 2026, with top LQ45 gainers and buy‑on‑weakness picks
body: The Jakarta Stock Exchange index (IHSG) closed up 1.69% at 6,373.85 on 12 August 2026, near the day’s high after having traded down to a low of 6,272.30 earlier. Among the LQ45 constituents, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk posted the strongest gain of 20.83% to Rp870, followed by PT Indosat Tbk (+14.42% to Rp2,460) and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (+7.14% to Rp1,950). Other notable gainers included PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk (+6.22% to Rp2,560), PT Darma Henwa Tbk (+5.43% to Rp466) and PT Hartadinata Abadi Tbk (+4.81% to Rp2,180). Declining stocks were PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (‑1.95% to Rp1,510), PT United Tractors Tbk (‑1.38% to Rp23,300) and PT Indika Energy Tbk (‑1.20% to Rp2,480). MNC Sekuritas recommended a buy‑on‑weakness approach for PT Barito Pacific Tbk, PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk, PT Timah Tbk and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk, while analysts noted support levels at 6,201 and 6,029 and resistance at 6,454 and 6,599.

title: Foreign investors net‑sell PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk and other stocks as the IHSG rose 1.69%
body: The article reports that despite the IHSG gaining 1.69% to 6,373.84 points on 12 August 2026, foreign investors recorded net sales in several Indonesian equities. The biggest net‑sell positions were in PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp 245.71 billion) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp 98.39 billion), followed by PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (Rp 30.96 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 27.94 billion), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (Rp 25.39 billion), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (Rp 24.88 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp 19.44 billion), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (Rp 19.32 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 17.38 billion) and PT Karya Pacific Energy Tbk (Rp 16.55 billion). Overall foreign investors posted a net buy jumbo of Rp 725.40 billion across the market, with 452 stocks advancing, 175 declining and 168 unchanged. The net‑sell activity highlights selective profit‑taking by foreigners even as the broader market rallied.

title: Foreign investors sell net Rp1.58 trillion of Indonesian stocks, top 10 net‑sell losers listed
body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.58 trillion in Indonesian equities from 10‑14 August 2026, with the biggest losers being PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp951.1 billion), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp766.8 billion), PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (Rp455.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp290.4 billion), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp238.7 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp118.5 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp86.4 billion), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (Rp73.4 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp68.4 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp66.2 billion), Kalbe Farma (Rp37.8 billion) and Darma Henwa (Rp35.9 billion). The outflows pressured the IHSG, which closed down 0.12 % at 6,401.89, while total market transactions fell 1.07 % to Rp15.21 trillion and trading volume dropped 14.86 % to 34.01 billion shares.

title: Astra International projected to improve in H2 2026 as automotive, financial services and Martabe mine drive growth
body: Analysts from Ciptadana Sekuritas Asia, BRI Danareksa Sekuritas and UBS Sekuritas Indonesia project that PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) will improve its performance in the second half of 2026. The outlook is based on a rebound in automotive revenue to Rp 66.1 trillion (up 5.9% YoY) and a 51% market share in four‑wheel vehicle sales, with Q2 net profit rising 14.2% QoQ to Rp 6.7 trillion. Strong financial‑services earnings, led by its financing arm PT Astra Sedaya Finance (net profit Rp 4.6 trillion), the restart of the Martabe gold mine, and diversification of PT United Tractors Tbk into metallurgical coal, together with an EPS growth forecast of 28.4% for FY26‑28, underpin the projection, while the company plans an Rp 8 trillion share buyback and a 45‑50% dividend payout. The three analysts each recommend a Buy rating with target prices of Rp 6,400, Rp 7,380 and Rp 6,850 per share, and the firm’s 2026 revenue and net‑profit forecasts are Rp 319.35 trillion and Rp 31.40 trillion respectively.

title: United Tractors' profit attributable to shareholders falls 88% YoY in H1 2026
body: United Tractors reported a sharp decline in profit attributable to its parent company in the first half of 2026. Profit attributable to shareholders dropped 88% year‑on‑year to Rp 956.28 billion, while net profit fell 91.13% to Rp 742.22 billion. Revenue decreased 14.94% to Rp 58.29 trillion, mainly due to a fall in goods sales from Rp 38.98 trillion to Rp 28.13 trillion, while service revenue remained roughly flat. Selling expenses rose to Rp 858.42 billion and general‑administrative expenses to Rp 3.92 trillion, and the company recorded a Rp 2.75 trillion impairment loss on joint‑venture investments and non‑operating receivables. Total assets grew modestly to Rp 179.06 trillion, with liabilities of Rp 77.31 trillion and equity of Rp 101.75 trillion.

title: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk reports 803% profit surge in H1 2026 driven by PT Arafura Surya Alam divestment and Penjom write-off
body: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk reported an 803% jump in profit attributable to its parent in the first half of 2026, reaching US$177.83 million (US$0,00067 per share) versus US$19.69 million a year earlier. The surge was driven by a US$298 million gain from the divestment of PT Arafura Surya Alam to PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara, a subsidiary of PT United Tractors Tbk, while sales rose 14.5% year‑on‑year to US$160.63 million. At the same time, PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk recorded a US$102.92 million write‑off of the Penjom gold mine, operated by its subsidiary J Resources Gold (UK) Ltd, which reduced the mine’s net book value to US$16.52 million and left the company with a pre‑tax loss of US$108.34 million before the divestment gain. As of 30 June 2026, total assets fell to US$636.86 million, cash and cash equivalents to US$17.06 million, and the firm invested US$195.35 million across currency‑linked investments, mutual funds and term deposits.

title: Heavy‑Equipment Market Projected to Grow, Yet PT United Tractors Tbk Sales Fall, PT Kobexindo Tractors Tbk Surge, and PT Intraco Penta Tbk Slip in Q2 2026
body: The article projects Indonesia’s heavy‑equipment market to keep expanding through 2026 but highlights divergent sales trends for three major issuers. PT Kobexindo Tractors Tbk reported a 47% year‑on‑year increase in Q2 2026 sales, while PT Intraco Penta Tbk saw an 11% decline and PT United Tractors Tbk’s first‑half 2026 sales dropped 27.83% YoY to Rp28.13 trillion from Rp38.98 trillion. UNTR’s Komatsu equipment sales rose 31% month‑on‑month to 399 units in July 2026, reaching a cumulative 2,393 units (59% of the annual estimate), and analysts note that KOBX’s diversification into non‑coal sectors supports its growth, whereas UNTR and INTA remain sensitive to RKAB adjustments. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas maintains a Buy rating on PT United Tractors Tbk with a target price of Rp30,600 and an Overweight stance, views PT Kobexindo Tractors Tbk as a growth‑oriented play, and advises caution on PT Intraco Penta Tbk pending operational improvements.

title: The Fate of Indonesian Stocks Amid MSCI's Whirlwind
body: MSCI Inc’s August 2026 index review, effective 1 September, removed GOTO and CPIN from the MSCI Global Standard, leaving nine Indonesian constituents: UNTR, BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BRMS, BBRI, BRPT, ASII and TLKM. During 1-2 September, foreign investors net bought the five most sought-after stocks—BBRI (Rp 993.29 bn), BBCA (Rp 589.83 bn), BMRI (Rp 227.78 bn), BBNI (Rp 36.34 bn) and BRPT (Rp 43.86 bn)—while net selling UNTR (Rp 10.11 bn), BRMS (Rp 54.06 bn), TLKM (Rp 111.7 bn) and ASII (Rp 65.92 bn). On the latest trading day, BBRI rose 0.30% to Rp 3,390, BBCA jumped 1.14% to Rp 6,675, BMRI gained 0.93% to Rp 4,360, BBNI climbed 0.78% to Rp 3,900 and BRPT slipped 0.55% to Rp 1,820, while ASII fell 1.63% to Rp 4,840, TLKM dropped 0.77% to Rp 2,590, BRMS declined 1.37% to Rp 720 and UNTR slipped 2.05% to Rp 25,050. The divergent net foreign flows underscore varying investor sentiment among the remaining MSCI constituents after the index composition change.

title: List of LQ45 stocks with lowest and highest PER on 2 September 2026, highlighting DEWA and AADI
body: The article lists the LQ45 index stocks with the lowest and highest price‑earnings ratios (PER) on 2 September 2026, highlighting PT Darma Henwa and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia. Trading volume fell as the total transaction value dropped to Rp16.8 trillion from Rp20.7 trillion, and foreign investors posted a net sell of 5.59 billion shares worth Rp326.6 billion. PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia declined 2.07% and PT Darma Henwa slipped 2.16%, while PT Amman Mineral Internasional fell 2.06%, PT United Tractors dropped 2.05%, PT Bukit Asam rose 1.87%, and PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper held the lowest price‑to‑book value at 0.38 times. PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, PT Bumi Resources, and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia were largely stagnant, and six other LQ45 constituents each weakened by less than 2%, all of which are members of the LQ45 index as noted in the article.

title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas Recommends Buy on PT United Tractors Tbk with Rp 30,600 Target Price on Operational Improvement
body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommended a buy rating on PT United Tractors Tbk with a target price of Rp 30,600, citing improving operational momentum in July 2026. The company's mining contractor subsidiary PAMA recorded coal production of 13 million tonnes, up 10% month-on-month, while Komatsu unit sales rose 31% to 399 units. Year-to-date through July, PAMA production and Komatsu sales reached 68% and 59% of full-year guidance, respectively, broadly in line with management targets. United Tractors shares traded at Rp 25,050 on September 2, 2026, down 2.05% on the day and 15.08% year-to-date, with a price-to-book value of 0.97 times. The brokerage positioned United Tractors as the best proxy for upward RKAB revisions, though flagged risk if Barito River water levels do not improve by October-November 2026.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk Reports Declining Seven-Month Sales Across Most Segments with July Improvement in Komatsu and PAMA
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), the heavy equipment and mining issuer of the Astra Group, recorded declining sales volumes across nearly all operational business lines for the first seven months of 2026. Its subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA), which runs the mining contractor business, saw client coal production fall 3.26% year-on-year to 80.1 million tons and overburden removal drop 10.07% to 572.5 million bcm. Subsidiary PT Tuah Turangga Agung (TTA), which operates the coal mining business, posted a 15.94% decline in sales to 7.98 million tons, while gold mining subsidiaries PT Agincourt Resources and PT Sumbawa Jutaraya reported a 77.62% plunge in equivalent gold sales to 32,000 ounces. For the first half of 2026, UNTR's net revenue fell 15% to Rp58.3 trillion and net profit attributable to the parent entity dropped 88% to Rp956 billion, though July monthly figures showed Komatsu sales rising to 399 units and PAMA overburden removal increasing to 90.9 million bcm.

title: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk Allocates Doup Divestment Proceeds to Foreign Currency Investments and Jumbo Dividend While Reporting Profit Driven by One-Time Gain
body: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk (PSAB) directed approximately half of the US$540 million proceeds from the February 2026 divestment of the Doup gold mine to PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) into Currency Linked Investments at DBS Bank Singapore, while allocating US$155.53 million to a jumbo dividend largely flowing to controller Jimmy Budiarto and US$165.2 million to repay bank and related-party debt. The investment, made through subsidiary PT J Resources Netherlands B.V. (JRN), recorded a US$6.73 million loss by June 30, 2026. PSAB reported a 803% year-on-year surge in first-half 2026 net profit to US$177.89 million, though the gain was almost entirely attributable to the US$298.6 million divestment profit; excluding this, the company would have posted a pre-tax loss of US$108.34 million driven by a US$102.92 million impairment at the Penjom mine in Malaysia and other write-downs. Despite the earnings quality concern, operational performance improved with revenue rising 14.5% to US$160.64 million and gross profit jumping 61% to US$141.69 million.

title: Foreign investors' top ten net‑buy stocks on 4 Sep 2026 amid a 0.47% IHSG correction
body: The article reports that foreign investors net bought ten Indonesian stocks on Friday 4 Sep 2026 while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) corrected 0.47% to 6,636.47. The market closed within a range of 6,633–6,704, with total share volume of 35.8 billion and transaction value of Rp 15.04 trillion, and foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 29.80 billion that day. Over the week, foreign investors accumulated a net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion, and the ten most purchased stocks were PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 196.83 billion), PT Timah Tbk (Rp 158.76 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 46.47 billion), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (Rp 33.6 billion), PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (Rp 25.27 billion), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (Rp 24.54 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 24.45 billion), PT Bukit Asam Tbk (Rp 19.11 billion), PT Sumber Global Energy Tbk (Rp 13.25 billion) and PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 10.43 billion). These companies were directly impacted by the foreign investors' net purchases, while the IHSG still posted a weekly gain of 1.82% despite the weekend correction.

title: United Tractors (UNTR) outlines 2026 plan for newly acquired PT Arafura Surya Alam gold mine
body: United Tractors (UNTR) disclosed its 2026 strategy for the newly acquired gold mining company PT Arafura Surya Alam (ASA). UNTR, through its subsidiaries PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and PT Energia Prima Nusantara, signed the agreement to acquire 100% of ASA in February 2026 from PT J Resources Nusantara for an enterprise value of US$540 million (Rp 8.8 trillion). The company will complete licensing, detailed engineering of a processing plant and phased land acquisition in 2026, with plant construction targeted for 2026‑2028 and first gold production expected in 2029. ASA’s Doup mine holds 1,571 koz of proven gold reserves and 3,107 koz of resources, implying an acquisition valuation of Rp 5.6 billion per koz of reserves and Rp 2.8 billion per koz of resources, below peer averages of Rp 10.9 billion and Rp 7.9 billion respectively.

title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
body: Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

title: UNTR Warns of El Niño Impact on Coal Mining as RKAB Revision Takes Effect
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) has warned that El Niño conditions in Kalimantan could affect its coal mining operations following the recent RKAB revision. The company reported a 23% drop in heavy‑equipment sales to 2,393 units in the first half of 2026, with big‑machine sales down 49% due to lower national coal RKAB quotas. Net consolidated income fell 15% to Rp58.3 trillion, and net profit excluding non‑recurring items fell 48% to Rp4.3 trillion, largely driven by weaker gold sales and pressure on the coal and heavy‑equipment segments. Overburden removal work also declined 10% to 573 million BCM, and coal production for client PAMA dropped 3% to 80 million tonnes.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk drives gold business as Martabe revives and Doup mine slated for 2029 operation
body: PT United Tractors Tbk is accelerating its gold‑mining diversification by resuming operations at the Martabe gold mine, managed by PT Agincourt Resources, in late May 2026 and by acquiring 100 % of PT Arafura Surya Alam through PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and PT Energi Prima Nusantara, with the Doup mine expected to start production in 2029. PT United Tractors Tbk projects Martabe to produce about 65,000 ounces of gold in 2026 after sales fell to 32,000 ounces in July 2026, while its first‑half 2026 consolidated net revenue dropped 15 % YoY to Rp58.28 trillion and net profit (excluding non‑recurring items) fell 48 % YoY to Rp4.3 trillion, pressured by a Rp3.3 trillion non‑recurring charge from a full impairment of its investment in Supreme Energy Rantau Dadap. Additional pressures came from a 23 % YoY decline in Komatsu equipment sales to 2,393 units and an 18 % YoY drop in coal sales of PT Tuah Turangga Agung to 6.5 million tonnes.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk projects challenging performance outlook through end of 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk said its operational outlook remains challenging through the end of 2026, with first‑half 2026 results showing pressure on both operations and an impairment charge. Net revenue for the first half fell 15% year‑on‑year to Rp 58.3 trillion, while net profit excluding non‑recurring items dropped 48% to Rp 4.3 trillion. The company recorded non‑recurring items of Rp 3.3 trillion, mainly an impairment on Supreme Geothermal Energy and payments related to forest‑area approvals at the Stargate nickel mine. Management expects the second half to improve on the back of higher coal‑mining output, a revised RKAB, stronger heavy‑equipment sales, mining‑contracting activity and a gradual recovery of the Martabe gold mine, although lower gold sales at PT Agincourt Resources contributed to the revenue decline.

title: UNTR reports 78% drop in gold sales and outlines future plans for Martabe and Doup mines
body: UNTR, a subsidiary of Grup Astra, said its gold sales fell 78% year‑on‑year to 32,000 ounces in the July‑2026 period, far below the 143,000 ounces sold in July 2025. The company projects total 2026 gold sales of 65,000 ounces, a 71.4% decline from 227,000 ounces in 2025, and expects the Martabe mine to operate at partial capacity after resuming in Q2 2026 while the Doup project, managed by PT Arafura Surya Alam, is slated for commercial production in 2029. UNTR’s revenue dropped 15% to Rp58.3 trillion and net profit plunged 88% after a Rp3.3 trillion fine and a write‑down of its investment in Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap, whose net capacity is 50‑52 MW versus the anticipated 90 MW. Its coal subsidiary PT Tuah Turangga Agung saw thermal coal sales rise 14% but metallurgical coal fall 18% amid a revised RKAB target of 9.6‑9.8 million tons for 2026.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk announces Doup gold mine will start production in 2029
