body: PT United Tractors Tbk announced that the Doup gold mine, operated by PT Arafura Surya Alam, will begin producing and selling gold in 2029 after its subsidiaries PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and PT Energia Prima Nusantara acquired 99,99996% of the mine from PT J Resources Nusantara and the remaining shares from Jimmy Budiarto and PT Mulia Bumi Persada in a US$540 million transaction. The company will focus on completing feasibility studies, environmental impact analysis, detailed engineering design for a processing plant, and phased land acquisition through 2028 to enable the 2029 production start.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk profit falls 48% as national coal RKAB allocation cuts weigh on heavy equipment and mining sales
body: PT United Tractors Tbk reported a 48% decline in profit for the first half of 2026, driven by reduced national coal RKAB allocations that dampened demand for its heavy‑equipment and mining‑contractor services. Heavy‑equipment sales of Komatsu United Tractors fell 23% year‑on‑year to 2,393 units, with big‑machine sales in mining down 49%, while overburden‑removal volumes for PAMA and KPP Mining dropped 10% to 573 million bcm and coal production for PAMA clients slipped 3% to 80 million tonnes. Gold sales from PT Agincourt Resources and PT Sumbawa Jutaraya collapsed 78% to 32,000 ounces, whereas nickel ore sales from PT Stargate Pacific Resources reached 973,000 wet metric tonnes, and spare‑parts and maintenance revenue rose 1% to Rp 5.5 trillion. Coal sales by PT Tuah Turangga Agung declined 18% to 6.5 million tonnes, reflecting the overall slowdown in the coal segment.

title: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analyst highlights expansion prospects and buy recommendations for PT Bumi Resources Tbk, PT Petrosea Tbk, PT United Tractors Tbk and PT Aneka Tambang Tbk.
body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analyst Abida Massi Armand reviews the overseas mining expansion of PT Bumi Resources Tbk, PT Petrosea Tbk, PT United Tractors Tbk and PT Aneka Tambang Tbk. PT Bumi Resources Tbk, via its subsidiary Bumi Resources Australia Pty Ltd, completed the acquisition of 100% of Loyal Metals Ltd for Rp 1,004,742,244,136.50 (AUD 79,069,731.75); PT Petrosea Tbk finalized a binding offer for Tolu Minerals Limited, issuing convertible notes worth AUS $23.75 million; PT United Tractors Tbk is exploring mineral asset acquisitions in Australia; and PT Aneka Tambang Tbk is targeting gold production in the Middle East. The analyst recommends buying PT Aneka Tambang Tbk with a target price of Rp 4,900 and PT United Tractors Tbk with a target price of Rp 30,600, noting strong free cash flow and diversification benefits. He cautions that integration risks, possible overpaying and regulatory hurdles may delay profit contributions for two to three years after the deals.

title: United Tractors Outlines H2 2026 Recovery Driven by RKAB Coal Quota Revision and Martabe Gold Mine Restart
body: PT United Tractors Tbk targets a gradual performance recovery in the second half of 2026, supported by the approval of a revised coal RKAB quota of 9.6–9.8 million tons for its subsidiary Tuah Turangga Agung and the resumption of the Martabe gold mine operated by Agincourt Resources, which aims to produce 65,000 ounces of gold this year. The company's first-half consolidated revenue fell 15% year-on-year to Rp58.3 trillion and net profit excluding non-recurring items dropped 48% to Rp4.3 trillion, weighed down by a Rp3.3 trillion full impairment on its investment in Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap. Analysts at BRI Danareksa highlight improving operational momentum, noting PAMA's coal production rose 10% month-on-month to 13 million tons in July and Komatsu sales surged 31% to 399 units, while Kiwoom Sekuritas points to a 400% quarterly jump in gold sales to 20,000 ounces in Q2 after Martabe restarted in mid-May. BRI Danareksa maintains a buy rating with a Rp30,600 target price, and UNTR shares closed up 1.4% at Rp25,300 on September 7, 2026, down 14.2% year-to-date but up 15% over the past three months.

title: Stock Recommendations to Watch When the IHSG Strengthens
body: The article highlights the performance of several stocks as the IHSG strengthens, noting that AMMN rose 5.90%, SMMA 5.26%, and MDKA 8.33%, while BELI fell 5.88%, BBNI 1.02%, and BREN 0.90%. Foreign investors net bought Rp379.39 billion in the regular market, and the Basic Materials sector gained 2.00% while Healthcare declined 0.59%. MDLA reported sales of Rp8.17 trillion and a 12.60% net profit increase to Rp225.63 billion, while BLOG posted revenue of Rp732.87 billion and a net profit of Rp77.54 billion, and PSAB announced a Rp30 per share interim dividend with a payout ratio of 24.93%. United Tractors (UNTR) is a subsidiary that received a divestment of the Doup gold mine, contributing to PSAB’s profit growth.

title: Astra International (ASII) Commits to 45-50% Dividend Payout Ratio for Fiscal Year 2026 Amid Mining Challenges
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) pledged to maintain a dividend payout ratio of 45% to 50% for fiscal year 2026, as stated by President Director Rudy at a public expose on September 10, 2026. The commitment comes despite first-half headwinds in coal and mineral mining, with net profit of Rp12.5 trillion on revenue of Rp157.9 trillion for H1 2026. Astra also approved a new share buyback program of up to Rp8 trillion for 12 months, while its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) announced a Rp2 trillion buyback for three months after its net profit plunged 88.2% year-on-year to Rp956.28 billion. Management expects a second-half recovery driven by the resumed operations of the Martabe gold mine in May 2026 and higher coal mining work plans, while automotive and financial services segments remained resilient with year-on-year growth of 9% and 6% respectively.

title: Astra Focuses on Three Core Profit Engines, Plans Rp35.6 Trillion Capex and VTO for AUTO, with Non-Fit Businesses Facing Capital Reallocation
body: Astra is sharpening its strategy around three core profit engines—automotive, financial services, and heavy equipment and mining solutions—which together contribute about 90% of group net profit. The company has earmarked Rp35.6 trillion in capital expenditure for 2026, of which Rp16.9 trillion has been realized in the first half, including Rp11.7 trillion for UNTR's acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam (Proyek Doup) mining assets and Rp5 trillion for routine spending. Astra is also preparing a voluntary tender offer (VTO) for AUTO shares at Rp3,600 per share, allocating Rp858 billion to potentially raise its stake to 84.95% and add an estimated Rp110–115 billion to net profit. Businesses that do not meet strategic-fit, ecosystem-contribution, and positive-performance criteria will face capital reallocation or divestment, while the remaining roughly Rp19 trillion of capex will be directed mainly to the three core segments. To support total shareholder return amid a 28% year-to-date share price decline, Astra maintains a 45–50% dividend payout ratio on recurring profit and plans an Rp8 trillion share buyback over the next year.

title: Astra International Explains Rationale for Voluntary Tender Offer to Increase Stake in Astra Otoparts
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed the reasoning behind its voluntary tender offer (VTO) to acquire up to 4.95% of PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) at Rp3,600 per share, citing confidence in AUTO's fundamental performance and long-term growth potential in automotive components. The acquisition, requiring up to Rp858 billion in internal funds, would raise ASII's ownership from 80% to 84.95% while maintaining the minimum 15% free float requirement. ASII President Director Rudi stated the additional 4.95% stake could contribute an estimated Rp110-115 billion annually to ASII's consolidated net profit, based on AUTO's projected annual net profit of Rp2.2-2.3 trillion. The move aligns with ASII's strategic focus since May 2026 on automotive, financial services, and mining solutions, with the company allocating Rp36 trillion for capital expenditure and strategic investments in 2026, including PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR)'s Rp11.7 trillion acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam.

title: Emtek subsidiary PT Kreatif Media Karya acquires 803.28 million shares of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, raising its stake to 45.68%
body: On Tuesday, 8 September, PT Kreatif Media Karya, an Emtek subsidiary, purchased 803.28 million shares of PT Bukalapak.com Tbk, increasing its ownership to 45.68%. The same filing shows Lo Kheng Hong buying 1 million shares of PT Intiland Development Tbk, lifting his holding to 7.51%, and Edwin Soeryadjaya acquiring 600 thousand shares of PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya Tbk, maintaining a 35.9% stake. Buyback actions were noted for PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (781,700 shares, 5.63% ownership), PT United Tractors Tbk (1.01 million shares, 7.77% ownership) and PT Arwana Citramulia Tbk (200,000 shares, 5.16% ownership). Additionally, CGS International Securities Singapore Pte Ltd sold 126 million shares of PT Wilton Makmur Indonesia Tbk, reducing its stake to 18.77%, while PT Bahana Nusantara Indojaya and PT Nusantara Makmur Lestari sold 2.55 million shares of PT Indokripto Koin Semesta Tbk (remaining 19.62%) and 205 thousand shares of PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (remaining 9.46%) respectively.

title: Astra International (ASII) Projects H2 2026 Earnings Recovery on Mining Rebound and Martabe Gold Mine Restart; ASII and Subsidiary United Tractors (UNTR) Announce Share Buybacks
body: Astra International (ASII) management expects a financial and operational recovery in the second half of 2026, driven by a rebound in the mining solutions and heavy equipment segment following the restart of the Martabe gold mine in May 2026 and an anticipated increase in coal mining work plans and budgets (RKAB). The automotive and financial services segments are projected to remain resilient throughout 2026. ASII reported a first-half 2026 net profit of Rp12.5 trillion on consolidated revenue of Rp157.9 trillion. Its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) posted a sharp 88.2% year-on-year decline in first-half net profit to Rp956.28 billion, with revenue falling 15% to Rp58.29 trillion, primarily due to lower gold sales at PT Agincourt Resources and weaker coal mining performance linked to a reduced national coal RKAB allocation. Both companies announced share buyback programs: ASII up to Rp8 trillion for 12 months approved on July 17, 2026, and UNTR up to Rp2 trillion for three months. Analysts at Stockbit believe UNTR can recover significantly in H2 2026 and that ASII still has a chance to meet the consensus full-year net profit estimate of around Rp29 trillion.

title: PT Astra International Tbk plans Rp36 trillion capex in 2026, allocating Rp15 trillion to PT United Tractors Tbk
body: On 10 September 2026, PT Astra International Tbk announced a total capital expenditure of Rp36 trillion for the year. The plan splits into Rp15 trillion of maintenance capex, primarily directed to PT United Tractors Tbk for mining solution and heavy-equipment projects, and Rp21 trillion of strategic investment capex. By the end of the first half of 2026, PT Astra International Tbk had spent Rp11.7 trillion on strategic investments and Rp5.2 trillion on maintenance capex, with most of the investment portion used to complete PT United Tractors Tbk’s acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam.

title: PT Astra International Tbk forecasts a recovery in the second half of 2026 and earmarks Rp36 trillion capex.
body: PT Astra International Tbk forecasts a recovery in the second half of 2026, noting resilience in its automotive and financial services segments and an expected rebound in mining solutions and heavy equipment. The group earmarked Rp36 trillion of capex for 2026—about Rp15 trillion for maintenance and Rp20-21 trillion for investment—spent Rp11.7 trillion on the acquisition of the gold mine Arafura Surya Alam melalui entitas grup United Tractors and Rp5.2 trillion on heavy-equipment purchases, and reported first-half consolidated net revenue of Rp157.9 trillion (down 3%) and net profit (excluding non-recurring items) of Rp14.9 trillion (down 7%).

title: IHSG Opens Weaker at Start of Week, Pressured by Global Sentiment
body: The IHSG opened 1.36% lower at 6,452 on Monday as rising oil prices above $100 per barrel and an 85% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting pressured sentiment. Foreign investors sold a net Rp2.31 trillion in the regular market, while trading volume reached 6.53 billion shares worth Rp3.06 trillion. Technical indicators show a hammer pattern at the 6,475-6,375 support zone with the index holding above its 20-day moving average at 6,533, suggesting a potential rebound. Brokerages offered divergent outlooks: BRI Danareksa sees a constructive bias targeting resistance at 6,600-6,700 and favors UNTR, IMPC, and TINS; Phintraco expects sideways movement between 6,450-6,700 and picks ANTM, ASII, EMAS, MDKA, and ISAT; CGS International forecasts varied gains with support at 6,465-6,390 and resistance at 6,620-6,695, recommending TAPG, AALI, ISAT, TINS, AMMN, and EMAS; Panin Sekuritas anticipates further weakness due to geopolitical tensions and foreign outflows, selecting INET, BRMS, and INCO.

title: Analysts Highlight Stocks Including COCO and RAJA
body: Amid a weakening IHSG, analysts from BRI Danareksa Sekuritas and MNC Sekuritas recommend several stocks for the next trading day on Tuesday (15/9/2026). Reza Diofanda of BRI Danareksa Sekuritas points to UNTR, targeting a rise to 26,875‑28,175 with support at 25,625; COCO, which broke out above its MA20, has a target of 146‑155 and support around 122‑128; and BBNI, rebounding above its MA20, is projected to climb to 3,960‑4,048 with support near 3,657. Herditya Wicaksana of MNC Sekuritas suggests MEDC, currently at 1,575 after a 1.29% gain, RAJA, down 2.44% to 800 and below its MA20, and SSMS, down 5.44% to 1,130, all positioned in specific Elliott wave phases. All three MNC Sekuritas picks—MEDC, RAJA, and SSMS—are recommended with a buy‑on‑weakness strategy.

title: PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) reaches Auto Reject Atas (ARA) at Rp13,825, outpacing transaction volumes of PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR)
body: On 18 September 2026, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (BYAN) surged 19.96% to Rp13,825 per share, hitting the Auto Reject Atas (ARA) level with a trade volume of 10.34 million shares valued at Rp142 billion, surpassing the transaction volumes of PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR). Earlier, on 16 September 2026, PT Jhonlin Baratama, acting for Haji Isam, signed a conditional share purchase agreement with BYAN’s controlling shareholders Low Tuck Kwong and Elaine Low to acquire 10,000,000,500 BYAN shares, representing roughly 30% of the outstanding equity and potentially granting majority control. At that time BYAN’s valuation metrics were a price‑to‑book ratio of 10.47×, a price‑to‑earnings ratio of 31×, and a market capitalisation of Rp460.83 trillion. For the first half of 2026, BYAN reported a 17% year‑on‑year net‑profit increase to US$410.25 million (Rp7 trillion) on revenue of US$1.74 billion (Rp31 trillion), while total assets rose to US$3.78 billion and equity declined to US$2.58 billion.

title: Pending RKAB revisions pressure mining‑service firms; Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia recommends PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR)
body: The article discusses how the lack of approval for revised RKAB plans through the end of 2026 creates selective pressure on mining‑service issuers, especially on work volume and heavy‑equipment utilization. Analyst Adrian Djie of Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia notes that contractors with diversified customers and commodities, such as those expanding into gold, nickel and non‑coal minerals, are better positioned, while firms dependent on a few quota‑constrained customers face greater risk. He also advises postponing capital expenditure on new equipment until production volumes for the second half of 2026 become clearer. Kiwoom Sekuritas Indonesia recommends buying PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) with a target price of Rp28,000 per share.

title: RKAB revision delays weigh on mining services issuers; analyst recommends UNTR
body: Delays in approving revised RKAB plans until September 2026, affecting about 50 mining companies, create uncertainty for mining services issuers. Analysts note that the 2026 coal production quota is projected at about 600 million tonnes, roughly 24 % lower than 2025, which could reduce contractors' work volume and pressure margins. PT Indo Premier Sekuritas analyst Brigita Kinari and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas analyst Abida Massi Armand stress diversification across commodities and recommend buying UNTR with a target price of Rp 30,600 per share. The impact of the RKAB delay is expected to be most felt in 2027, with diversified issuers likely to recover faster.

title: Shareholding changes above 5% on 18 Sep: Dato Tahir reduces MPRO stake to 10.49% and notable transactions in NSSS, YULE, JECX, MAPI, PRDA and UNTR
body: On 18 Sep, Dato Tahir sold 37 million shares of PT Maha Properti Indonesia Tbk (MPRO), lowering his ownership from 10.86% to 10.49%. In PT Nusantara Sawit Sejahtera Tbk (NSSS), Samuel International divested 534.17 million shares (down to 12.9%), PT Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia sold 611.33 million shares (down to 14.06%), PT Nusantara Makmur Lestari cut its holding to about 9.46%, while PT Samuel Tumbuh Bersama bought 3.59 billion shares, raising its stake to 36.75%. Sabrina Evelyn Elian increased her holding in PT Yulie Sekuritas Indonesia Tbk (YULE) to 5.18%; Emtek, through PT Sarana Meditama Metropolitan Tbk (SAME), added 413 000 shares of PT Nitrasanata Dharma Tbk (JECX) to a 32.95% stake, and Samudra (Investment) Pte. Ltd. purchased 2.35 million shares of PT Mitra Adiperkasa Tbk (MAPI), bringing its ownership to 30.08%. The session ended with buybacks: PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk (PRDA) repurchased 404 400 shares, holding 6.24% of its stock, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) bought back 464 600 shares, holding 7.84%.

title: Stock Moves of Salim to Prajogo Conglomerate Issuers: Who Delivered the Highest Returns?
body: The article reviews the year‑to‑date (YTD) share‑price performance of issuers affiliated with Salim Group, Astra Group and Prajogo Pangestu group in 2026. Salim affiliates PT PP London Sumatra Indonesia Tbk (LSIP) surged 36.82% to Rp1,635, reporting 16% revenue growth to Rp2.69 trillion and a 25% net‑profit rise to Rp891 billion, while PT Salim Ivomas Pratama Tbk (SIMP) and PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) posted gains of 7.89% to Rp615 and 3.32% to Rp7,000 respectively. Astra affiliates PT Astra Otoparts Tbk (AUTO) climbed 25.28% to Rp3,370 with revenue up 13.2% to Rp10.9 trillion and net profit up 22.6% to about Rp1.15 trillion, PT Astra Agro Lestari Tbk (AALI) rose 13.22% to Rp8,350, and PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) fell 16.27% to Rp24,700. Prajogo Pangestu affiliates PT Petrosea Tbk (PTRO) dropped 50.57% to Rp5,400 despite a 59.56% revenue jump to US$543.98 million, and PT Barito Pacific Tbk (BRPT) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (CUAN) also slumped sharply, underscoring weaker YTD returns for the Prajogo group.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) posts 21.09% YoY drop in Komatsu equipment sales and sharp declines in gold and nickel output in August 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) recorded a 21.09% year‑on‑year decline in Komatsu heavy‑equipment sales, delivering 2,689 units in the January‑August 2026 period versus 3,408 units a year earlier. Mining accounted for 52% of those sales, while August alone saw 296 units sold, a 32.58% month‑on‑month drop from July’s 399 units. Overburden removal through PT Pamapersada Nusantara fell 8.46% YoY to 670.2 million bcm and coal sales via PT Tuah Turangga Agung slipped 19.44% YoY to 8.37 million tons, while gold sales from Agincourt Resources and Sumbawa Jutaraya fell 73.91% YoY to 42,000 ounces and nickel ore sales via Stargate declined to 1.05 million wet metric tons. The data, reported on 23 September, highlights weakening demand across UNTR’s mining‑related equipment and mineral‑product segments.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex realization of Rp 17 trillion, 47.2% of annual target
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said that in the first half of 2026 it has realized about Rp 17 trillion of its planned Rp 36 trillion capex, representing roughly 47.2% of the yearly target. The bulk of the realized capex was used for the acquisition of the gold mine PT Arafura Surya Alam by PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR). The remaining portion funded routine capital spending, mainly the purchase of heavy equipment to support United Tractors’ mining contractor operations. The company indicated that the balance of the capex budget will be allocated more selectively and disciplined to sustain future business growth, with ongoing evaluation.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) reports coal production and heavy equipment sales fall as RKAB approvals lag
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) said its coal production and heavy equipment sales have declined because the government has not fully approved its Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya (RKAB). The company has a total coal production capacity of 15 million tons but only 7.4 million tons of RKAB were approved in the first half of 2026, about 50% of capacity, later rising to 12.4 million tons in August. Coal sales from January to August 2026 fell 22% to 6,723 tons, while heavy equipment sales dropped 21% to 2,689 units, with big‑machine sales halving to 436 units from 860 a year earlier. The downturn is also linked to El Nino‑induced dry conditions in Central Kalimantan, and the company expects coal sales to improve in the November‑December quarter.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) feels impact of RKAB policy on coal operations and revenue
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) said the Rencana Kerja dan Anggaran Biaya (RKAB) policy continues to pressure its mining operations through August 2026. Coal production at its subsidiary Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA) fell 3% year‑on‑year to 96.2 million tons, overburden removal dropped 8% to 670.2 million bcm and the stripping ratio slipped to 7.2 from 7.6. Revenue for the six‑month period ended 30 June 2026 declined 15% to IDR 5.8 trillion, while PAMA’s revenue still grew and a higher nickel price and a stronger US dollar partially offset the volume weakness. UNTR, which has a coal production capacity of 15 million tons, increased its approved RKAB to 12.4 million tons in August and is cutting capex and prioritising spending to navigate the dry season in Central Kalimantan.

title: UNTR's RKAB approval delayed, new coal production allocation set at 12.4 million tons
body: PT Unit d Tractors Tbk (UNTR) said its approved coal production capacity under the RKAB was reduced to 7.4 million tons, about half of the original 15 million‑ton target, due to a delayed RKAB approval process. The company also reported a 22 percent drop in coal sales in the first eight months of 2026, but noted that an August allocation increased its RKAB capacity to 12.4 million tons.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) reports coal production and heavy‑equipment sales decline as RKAB approval is cut by 50%
body: UNTR’s coal production capacity of 15 million tons was limited to 7.4 million tons under the government‑approved RKAB, resulting in a 22 % year‑on‑year drop in coal sales to 6,723 tons for the January‑August 2026 period. The same RKAB reduction also cut Komatsu heavy‑equipment sales by 21 % to 2,689 units, with big‑machine sales falling from 860 to 436 units, while the company expects RKAB to rise to 12.4 million tons in August 2026 and anticipates production recovery in November‑December 2026 despite El Nino‑related challenges.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports capex absorption of Rp17 trillion in the first half of 2026
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) said it has realized about Rp17 trillion of its planned Rp36 trillion capital expenditure for 2026 by the end of the first semester. The realized capex includes the acquisition of the gold mine PT Arafura Surya Alam, which was carried out by PT United Tractors Tbk. The remaining budget is split into Rp15 trillion for maintenance capex and Rp21 trillion for strategic investments, as outlined by President Director Rudi. PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) indicated that future capex allocations will be evaluated to ensure they support business productivity and growth.

title: RKAB Dampens Heavy Equipment Sales, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) Impacted
body: RKAB, the mining work-plan and budget policy, is curbing heavy equipment purchases, hitting PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) and its subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA). UNTR's Komatsu equipment sales fell 21% to 2,689 units (big-machine sales down 49% to 436 units) in the first eight months of 2026, while PAMA’s overburden removal and coal production activity slipped 8%, though UNTR’s parts and service revenue rose 1% to about Rp5.5 trillion, offsetting some pressure.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) reports first‑half 2026 capex of Rp 17 trillion, driven by subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR).
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) disclosed that it has realized approximately Rp 17 trillion of capital expenditure in the first half of 2026, out of a total planned capex of Rp 35‑36 trillion for the year. The majority of the spending was incurred by its subsidiary PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), primarily for the acquisition of the Arafura Surya Alam gold mine and for routine purchases of heavy equipment for its mining contractor business. Astra indicated that the remaining capex budget will be allocated in a disciplined manner to support productivity and profit growth through 2027. The company said it will continue periodic evaluations to ensure the capex contributes optimally to earnings growth.

title: RKAB increases to 12.4 million tons, PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) aims to boost coal production in the second half of 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) raised its coal RKAB quota from about 7.4 million tons to 12.4 million tons in August 2026, giving the company a chance to boost output in the second half of the year. UNTR plans to schedule production and sales for November–December 2026 while holding some inventory, despite weather challenges from El Nino in Central Kalimantan. Coal sales through PT Tuah Turangga Agung reached 8.37 million tons in Jan–Aug 2026, a 19.44 % YoY decline from 10.39 million tons, while gold sales from Agincourt Resources and Sumbawa Jutaraya fell 73.91 % YoY to 42 000 ounces and nickel ore sales via Stargate dropped to 1.05 million wet metric tons (711 000 limonite, 348 000 saprolite) from 1.43 million tons in 2025. Coal production for UNTR’s customers via PT Pamapersada Nusantara also slipped 2.91 % YoY to 93.4 million tons.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) earmarks Rp7.1 trillion for share buyback through June 2026
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR), a subsidiary of Astra International, has earmarked a total of Rp7.1 trillion for share repurchases from July 2022 through 30 June 2026. The company completed a buyback of 35.5 million shares between 1 April and 30 June 2026 and will be able to repurchase up to Rp2 trillion of shares between 1 July and 30 September 2026. To date, UNTR has bought back 239 million shares worth Rp7.1 trillion, while its stock has fallen 17.46% year‑to‑date and trades in a range of Rp20,125 to Rp32,825 per share. The buyback aims to reinforce investor confidence and stabilize the share price amid market volatility.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) receives approval to raise coal RKAB to 12.4 million tons
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) announced that the government approved an increase in its coal work plan and budget (RKAB) to 12.4 million tons, still below its 15‑million‑ton production capacity. The new RKAB level exceeds the 7.4‑million‑ton plan approved for the first half of 2026. UNTR reported that coal sales fell 22 % to 6,723 tons and heavy‑equipment sales dropped 21 % to 2,689 units in the January‑August 2026 period, with big‑machine sales declining to 436 units from 860 units a year earlier. The company attributed the slowdown to the limited RKAB and El Nino‑related production constraints in Central Kalimantan, projecting that coal sales will only return to optimal levels in November‑December.

title: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) realizes Rp17 trillion capex in H1 2026.
body: PT Astra International Tbk (ASII) has realized about Rp17 trillion in capital expenditure (capex) for the first half of 2026, representing roughly 47.2% of its annual capex budget of Rp36 trillion. The realized capex is being used to fund PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR)’s acquisition of the gold mine PT Arafura Surya Alam. With the Rp17 trillion spend, ASII still has approximately Rp19 trillion of capex remaining for the rest of 2026, and the group’s total capex for the year is projected at Rp35.6 trillion. The three core business segments continue to contribute about 89% of Astra’s net profit and revenue, underscoring the focus of the capex allocation. On the day of the announcement, ASII shares fell 0.63% to Rp4,750, marking a 2.46% decline over five days and a 30.15% drop since the start of 2026.

title: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) raises coal RKAB to 12.4 million tons and continues to boost mineral mining business
body: PT United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) revised its coal work‑and‑budget plan to 12.4 million tons for August 2026, up from about 7.4 million tons, while Jan‑Aug 2026 coal sales fell 19.4% YoY to 8.37 million tons and gold and nickel sales dropped 73.9% to 42,000 ounces and 1.05 million wet metric tons respectively. JP Morgan Sekuritas, the equity research firm that issued an overweight rating, projects $330 million excess free cash flow in 2027, maintains a Rp 2 trillion quarterly buyback and a Rp 30,200 target price for June 2027, as the stock traded at Rp 24,400 on 23 Sept.

title: United Tractors' long journey toward a sustainable industry
body: United Tractors Tbk (UNTR) is pursuing a transformation to balance its coal and non‑coal businesses to 50:50 by 2030 and cut greenhouse‑gas emissions 30% by that year. The company is optimizing its core through subsidiary PT Pamapersada Nusantara (PAMA), which has adopted ERP S/4HANA and Mine Image Recognition, while diversifying into nickel via subsidiary PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara (DTN) smelter and gold via subsidiary PT Agincourt Resources (PTAR) with biodiversity‑focused ESG due diligence. Renewable‑energy efforts are channeled through subsidiary PT Energi Prima Nusantara (EPN), which holds a 31.49% stake in PT Arkora Hydro Tbk (ARKO) operating 27.4 MW of hydro capacity and 15.4 MW under construction, alongside floating solar projects, geothermal exploration via PT Supreme Energy Rantau Dedap (SERD) and waste‑to‑energy partnerships. Up to 30 June 2026, UNTR reported net revenue of Rp58.28 trillion and net profit of Rp956 billion, with segment revenues of Rp14.97 trillion (heavy equipment), Rp27.16 trillion (mining contractor), Rp12.86 trillion (thermal & metallurgical coal) and Rp2.35 trillion (non‑coal mineral mining); emissions intensity fell to 12.03% in 2025 and renewable‑energy consumption rose to 23.99 million GJ, including 15,298.56 GJ from solar.
